name: @projexlight/contracts
summary: Typed source of truth for ProjexCloud — TypeScript interfaces, event envelopes (UsageEvent.v1, AuditEvent.v1, six-layer JWT claims), DTO shapes, error codes. Every SDK + service imports from here so cross-package contracts stay in lockstep. Pure declarative — no runtime code beyond barrel exports.

scenarios.title: Import a canonical event envelope shape
scenarios.when_to_use: Any SDK emitting or consuming UsageEvent.v1 / AuditEvent.v1 / SixLayerJwtClaims — import the type instead of redeclaring.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Type compiles. Cross-SDK shape stays in lockstep — bumping the contract version cascades the type change to every consumer at build time.

scenarios.title: Use the canonical error-code enum
scenarios.when_to_use: Any service emitting structured errors — use the shared ErrorCode union so consumers can switch on the same set.
scenarios.example_code:
import { ErrorCode } from '@projexlight/contracts';
throw new HttpError({ code: ErrorCode.HARD_CAP_DENIED });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Consumers across SDKs handle the same code. No drift between services.

scenarios.title: Add a new event v2 alongside v1
scenarios.when_to_use: Schema evolution — never mutate v1; declare v2 alongside. Consumers migrate at their own cadence.
scenarios.example_code: // in this package: export interface UsageEventV2 extends Omit<UsageEventV1, 'dimensions'> { dimensions: ExtendedDimensions; }
scenarios.expected_outcome: Old + new event shapes coexist. CI gate refuses any v1 mutation that would break consumers.

compliance_posture.notes: Pure types — no runtime behavior. Contract changes pass through the same PR review that gates schema migrations.
